pomodoro-timer.quickAnswer: The Pomodoro technique splits work into 25-minute focus sessions separated by 5-minute breaks, with a 15-minute break after every 4 sessions. Set your lengths, press start, and the timer cycles automatically while counting completed sessions. One full cycle is 100 minutes of focused work with 30 minutes of breaks.
keyFacts: The classic Pomodoro is 25 minutes of focus, 5 minutes of rest, repeated 4 times, then a 15-minute long break.
Short, fixed sprints beat vague 'work all afternoon' plans because the finish line is always near.
The timer advances automatically: focus -> short break -> focus ... -> long break -> focus.
Session lengths are fully adjustable - students often prefer 50/10, writers 25/5.
Counting completed sessions turns an abstract day into visible progress.
howTo: Set your focus length (default 25 minutes) and break lengths.
Choose after how many sessions the long break comes (default 4).
Press Start and work on one task until the timer ends the session.
Rest during breaks - step away from the screen.
Press Reset anytime to start a fresh sequence.
pomodoro-timer.formula:
One cycle = N focus sessions + (N - 1) short breaks + 1 long break.
Focus time per cycle = N x focus length.
Break time per cycle = (N - 1) x short + 1 x long.
Classic: 4 x 25 + 3 x 5 + 15 = 100 min focus + 30 min breaks.
pomodoro-timer.workedExample:
Classic settings: 25 / 5 / 15, long break after 4.
1. Session 1: 25 min focus -> 5 min break.
2. Session 2: 25 min focus -> 5 min break.
3. Session 3: 25 min focus -> 5 min break.
4. Session 4: 25 min focus -> 15 min long break.
5. Totals: 100 minutes of focus, 30 minutes of rest, 4 completed sessions.
benefits: Turns big scary tasks into small finishable sprints.
Regular breaks protect focus and reduce end-of-day burnout.
Adjustable lengths fit studying, coding, writing or housework.
No account, no tracking - just a clean timer.
limitations: Browser timers can drift slightly and pause in background tabs; treat it as a guide, not a lab instrument.
There is no alarm sound - keep the tab visible or check back.
The technique suits solo focused work best; meetings cannot be Pomodoro'd.
Changing settings mid-run is disabled to protect the current session - pause or reset first.

faqs.a: A time-management method: work in focused 25-minute sprints with 5-minute breaks, taking a longer 15-minute break after every 4 sprints. It was named after a tomato-shaped kitchen timer.
Yes - set any focus, short-break and long-break lengths before starting. Many people prefer 50/10 for deep work.
Yes. When a focus session ends it moves to a break, and when a break ends it returns to focus, counting completed sessions.

faqs.q: What should I do during breaks?
faqs.a: Step away from the screen: stretch, drink water, look outside. Avoid starting another task - the break is the point.

faqs.q: Why is there no sound alarm?
faqs.a: This version is intentionally simple and works without audio permissions. Keep the tab visible to catch phase changes.

faqs.q: Does it keep running if I close the tab?
faqs.a: No - the timer lives in the page. Closing or reloading the tab resets it.
